name: Q1422+2309 field, pointing 1 (Hubble)
blurb: A deep field toward the lensed quasar Q1422+2309, seen by Hubble.
label: q14221ir-hubble
story: One of several pointings in a survey field around a lensed quasar, where astronomers hunt for star-forming galaxies that let ionizing light escape, the light thought to have reionized the early universe. Hubble's sharp view helps separate those distant galaxies from nearer ones that sit along the same line of sight.

claims.text: The Q1422+2309 field is a Lyman break galaxy survey field centered on a gravitationally lensed quasar
Hubble program 15287 imaged the Q1422 field to study galaxies at z~3 that may leak Lyman-continuum (ionizing) radiation
Escaping ionizing radiation from star-forming galaxies is thought to have driven cosmic reionization
The Hubble imaging is used to remove contamination from lower-redshift foreground galaxies
